title: Covenant: Abraham and Moses
welcome_lead: From Ur of the Chaldeans to Sinai, follow the covenants that founded the Jewish people.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: Abraham, Moses, the Exodus and the Sinai covenant.
final_note: You have followed the covenantal story with respect. Jewish life is structured by mitzvot and memory.

concepts.def: Binding agreement initiated by God with chosen partners — Noah, Abraham, Moses, David.
Patriarch with whom God established a covenant (Genesis 12, 15, 17) and the rite of circumcision.
Leader who delivered the Israelites from Egypt and received the Torah at Sinai.
Liberation of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt, commemorated annually at Passover.
Covenant at Mount Sinai including the Ten Commandments and the Torah.
Commandments — traditionally 613 (248 positive and 365 negative) — structuring Jewish life.

walkthroughs.body_html: God's call to Abraham (Genesis 12) and the covenant of Genesis 15 and 17 promise land, descendants and blessing. Circumcision (brit milah) on the eighth day after birth marks the covenant in male children. Abraham's faithfulness, including the binding of Isaac (Akedah), is central to Jewish theology.

Moses encounters God at the burning bush (Exodus 3), leads the Israelites from Egypt and through the parting of the Sea of Reeds. The journey culminates at Mount Sinai with the giving of the Torah and the Ten Commandments. Passover (Pesach) commemorates the Exodus annually.

Tradition counts 613 mitzvot in the Torah, including dietary laws (kashrut), Sabbath observance and ethical duties summarised by Hillel as 'love your neighbour'. Halakhah, Jewish law as developed in rabbinic literature, articulates how mitzvot are applied today.
